name: Austria-Hungary

areaKm2.note: world_1914 Austro-Hungarian Empire polygon = ~650,000 km2 computed on the sphere (low); published area incl. Bosnia ~676,600 km2 (B&H Table 2: 0.6M km2).

population.note: Broadberry and Harrison 2005 Table 2: Austria-Hungary 1913 = 50.6M (low); COW tpop 1914 = 52,594k (high). Includes Bosnia-Herzegovina.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share 1910: Austria 40%, Hungary 25.6% (present-day borders; the Galician and Balkan lands were far less urban). Mid 0.25 for the empire. Low = COW upop/tpop 1914 = 4,405/52,594 = 0.08 (cities over 100,000).

activePersonnel.note: Cited page: after war was declared 3.35 million men (incl. the first call-up of the reserves and the 1914 recruits) gathered for action. Navy (~20,000 peace, ~35,000 mobilised) included. Snapshot month: August 1914. Check: COW NMC v7 milper 1914 = 839k, 1915 = 3,800k (annual averages, not the snapshot-date strength).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Rothenberg, The Army of Francis Joseph (isbn:0-911198-41-5), not read from a fetched source. Trained Landsturm and Ersatz reservists not called in August; low conscription (only ~20-25% of each class trained, Rothenberg ch. 10) left a small trained pool.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Rothenberg, The Army of Francis Joseph (isbn:0-911198-41-5), not read from a fetched source. Artillery, engineers, trains (the B-Staffel shuttle between Serbia and Galicia), fortress garrisons (Przemysl ~130,000), Landsturm rear units, navy, staffs.

mobilizationRatio.note: Total mobilised: 9,000,000 (Austrian government reply to the ILO) or 7,800,000 (US War Dept) on the cited page; / ~51.5M = 0.15-0.175.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Rothenberg, The Army of Francis Joseph (isbn:0-911198-41-5), not read from a fetched source. 48 infantry divisions of the common army, Landwehr and Honved plus Landsturm brigades (~12,000 rifles per division) and march battalions. Reconstruction from Rothenberg ch. 11 and Herwig ch. 2.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Mannlicher M95 and Schwarzlose MG good; fewest guns per division of the powers (~42)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: short-service conscripts, ~20-25% of each class trained; officers could not speak their men's languages

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Rothenberg, The Army of Francis Joseph (isbn:0-911198-41-5), not read from a fetched source. Tiroler Kaiserjaeger (4 regiments), Landesschuetzen (3 regiments) and ~32 Feldjaeger battalions.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: mountain equipment

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: elite mountain and rifle units

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Rothenberg, The Army of Francis Joseph (isbn:0-911198-41-5), not read from a fetched source. 11 cavalry divisions (hussars, dragoons, uhlans) plus divisional squadrons.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: colourful uniforms, saddles that galled the horses; cavalry ruined in the August 1914 reconnaissance

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: regular cavalry

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. ~42 guns per infantry division (Herwig ch. 2) for ~48 divisions, plus horse, mountain and corps heavy artillery and the Skoda 30.5 cm siege mortars; ~3,000-4,000 field and heavy pieces. Fortress guns excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: obsolescent 8 cm M5 bronze-steel field guns; excellent Skoda heavy mortars

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: poor co-operation with infantry in Serbia and Galicia

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. Luftfahrtruppen ~40 aircraft and a few airships in August 1914 (Herwig ch. 2). Reconnaissance types; the first aircraft rammed in air combat was Austrian (Aviation in WWI page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Lohner and Etrich types

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: tiny air arm

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Battleships, cruisers and destroyers. Conway's 1906-1921: 3 Tegetthoff dreadnoughts (Szent Istvan 1915), 3 Radetzky, 3 Erzherzog Karl, 3 Habsburg and 3 Monarch-class coast-defence battleships; 2-3 armoured and ~7 light/protected cruisers (Novara class, Admiral Spaun, Zenta, Aspern...) = 22/26/28; plus 6 Tatra and 12 Huszar-class destroyers = 18. Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor.

quality.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.65/0.7/0.75 (26) and destroyers 0.6/0.65/0.7 (18), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric rows: quality 0.75 and 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Tegetthoff the first triple-turret dreadnoughts; modern Novara scouts; Tatra class fast and well armed

training.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.55/0.6/0.65 (26) and destroyers 0.6/0.65/0.7 (18), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: multinational crews, fleet kept in harbour (fleet in being); destroyers active in Adriatic raiding

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Torpedo boats only: ~27 250 t sea-going torpedo boats, counted in the high bound only. The 18 destroyers (6 Tatra, 12 Huszar) moved to ships_major (was 18/18/25), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Tatra class fast and well armed

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Adriatic raiding

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. U-1 to U-6 (U-12 taken over in August 1914).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: small boats (U-5 class teardrop hull, cited navy page)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: U-5 sank the French cruiser Leon Gambetta in 1915

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Conrad split his army between Serbia and Galicia and lost both opening campaigns; Potiorek beaten by the Serbs; staff trained but plans unrealistic

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: eleven nationalities, German command language; held surprisingly well in 1914 but lost most of its regular officers by year end

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5. Evidence: loyal dynastic mobilisation in 1914; Czech and Serb units less reliable

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: Mannlicher M95, Schwarzlose MG, Skoda 30.5 cm mortars; obsolete field guns

armor.note: Anchor: 7 (armoured cars, steel helmet 1915). Evidence: no helmets or armour in 1914

ships.note: Anchor: 7 (dreadnoughts). Evidence: Tegetthoff dreadnoughts, modern scouts and destroyers

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 (concrete forts). Evidence: Przemysl, Krakow, Tyrolean plateau forts in concrete

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways). Evidence: adequate network but slow trains; the B-Staffel went to Serbia and back to Galicia

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (telegraph, telephone). Evidence: telephone and telegraph; language barriers; Austrian codebreakers read Russian radio

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 7 = aerial reconnaissance. Evidence: cavalry reconnaissance failed in August 1914; few aircraft

gdpPerCapita.note: B&H Table 2: 1,986 in 1990 int$; x ~1.6 (the 2011/1990 int$ ratio of Maddison 2023 vs 2001 for Germany and France) = ~3,180. Cross-check, population-weighted Maddison 2023 (OWID CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv) 1913 values: Austria 5,523 (6.6M), Czech lands ~3,800 (10M), Hungary 3,344 (7.7M), Slovakia/Transylvania/Croatia ~2,200 (12M), Galicia/Bukovina ~2,000 (8.8M), Bosnia/Dalmatia ~1,500 (2.5M) = ~3,110.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Ferguson, The Pity of War (isbn:0-7139-9246-8), not read from a fetched source. Low: defence ~2.8% of NNP in 1913, the lowest of the great powers (Ferguson table 6). Mid/high: wartime share; B&H Table 5 gives no Austro-Hungarian government series.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry and mining ~30% of output, concentrated in Bohemia, Lower Austria and Budapest; Galicia and the south-east agrarian.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment. Cited page: 67% of the workforce in agriculture in 1870 and 60% in 1913. 1 - 0.60 = 0.40 (mid). The Austrian half depended on Hungarian grain.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Rothenberg, The Army of Francis Joseph (isbn:0-911198-41-5), not read from a fetched source. Men reaching 21 per year ~0.45-0.55M; only ~160,000-200,000 per year were actually inducted before 1912 (Rothenberg ch. 10).

artillery.note: Educated guess. Field and heavy guns per year 1915-1917 (Skoda Pilsen, Steyr; output limited by steel and coal).

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Fighters per year 1916-1917 (Hansa-Brandenburg D.I, Aviatik D.I, Albatros licence); total Austro-Hungarian aircraft output ~5,400 over the war.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Reconnaissance and bomber aircraft per year 1915-1917.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Szent Istvan completed 1915; no capital ships after.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Destroyers and large torpedo boats per year.

submarines.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Submarines completed per year 1915-1918 (~25 over the war).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Metalled roads of Austria and Hungary; poor in Galicia and the Carpathians.

railKm.note: Educated guess. CHAT railline Austria 1913 = 22,981 km (Cisleithania, read from https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta); CHAT has no Hungarian value before 1921, so the Hungarian and Bosnian lines (~22,000 km) are recalled.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Trieste, Pola, Fiume, Cattaro, Sebenico, Spalato.

merchantTonnage.note: Lloyd's Register returns 1914: Austro-Hungarian flag 1,011,414 GRT (steam and sail, 100 tons and over, Register Book 1913-14). Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (low x1.3 of the low GRT, high x1.6 of the high GRT).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Austro-Hungarian armies in Serbia and Galicia struggled beyond ~100-150 km of the railheads; Carpathian winter campaign 1915 a logistic disaster.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses of Austria (~1.8M) and Hungary (~2.3M) plus Bosnia; ~0.6M requisitioned in 1914.

chokepoints: Danube and Sava crossings at Belgrade

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: Carpathian and Alpine barriers, fortresses (Przemysl, Krakow), population support in the core lands.

notes: Snapshot date August 1914 after mobilisation (partial mobilisation against Serbia 25 July, general 31 July). Territory = the Dual Monarchy incl. Bosnia-Herzegovina; includes is empty (Austria and Hungary as later states are separate nationIds). Forces are the whole army; ~1M men went to Galicia against Russia and ~0.3M against Serbia in August (Herwig ch. 2). Aircraft in aircraft_strike (no fighters in 1914). Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Book figures (Rothenberg, Herwig, Conway's) not fetched online, graded at most B.
